feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong career progression at NACo and a well-aligned headline/profile.  
- Good credibility: specific platforms, tools, scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and mission-driven context.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain vocabulary and consistent emphasis on cross-channel leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or team size/budget managed.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize punctuation in bullets and date formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, a more concise opening, and one or two concrete signals of scale or sector relevance.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing: change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience,” and reduce generic wording like “expert in.”
- Lead with current market positioning: emphasize digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications earlier.
- Add specificity tied to the CV, such as enterprise web platforms, cross-functional governance, or advocacy/member-facing organizations.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams and large-scale digital operations. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” closely overlap with Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- Avoid adding tool names or detailed platform examples here; those are already covered well in skills and experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value leadership and systems strengths over generic phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and elevate wording: “Digital strategy & transformation” → “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Replace generic or overlapping items with more distinctive strengths, e.g.: “CMS modernization,” “Digital governance,” “Audience analytics & KPI reporting,” “Content operations & editorial systems.”
- Consider a more targeted version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization • Content operations & editorial systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • Audience analytics & KPI reporting • Digital governance • Advocacy & policy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep style consistent: use plural “communications” and parallel noun phrases throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” and “Editorial workflow design” are close; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the projects footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this senior level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and client scope: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate bullets into 4–5 sharper points; combine overlapping web/platform language. Example: “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource hubs.”
- Add measurable outcomes wherever possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search success/engagement gains, or stakeholder teams enabled.
- Reframe AI/search bullet to show leadership and result: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep one high-level mention here and leave technical detail to Projects.
- Governance/analytics/workflows echoes NACo roles; emphasize freelance embedded leadership and new platform builds instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, channel management is framed through outcomes, and older NACo responsibilities are not repeated.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national association serving county officials.”
- Lead with the highest-impact achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Rephrase channel oversight to emphasize scale/results, not just ownership: include email audience size, engagement growth, campaign performance, or follower growth if available.
- Tighten remaining bullets to outcome language: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…,” “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack…,” “Established governance and publishing standards that improved cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as building organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “strengthened workflows/governance” too closely; the Director role already covers governance and standards at a higher level.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing leadership scope and strategic outcomes rather than repeating generic skill phrases.

Suggested edit
- Tighten to 4 sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and audience strategy
- Replace “audience-focused content planning” with “audience strategy” or “content operations” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning language styles.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) for recent experience bullets, not this skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older items unless central to target roles; consider removing “jQuery” and possibly “WordPress” if Drupal/public-sector modernization is the stronger recent story.
- Group Microsoft tools together if kept: “SharePoint / Power Pages” rather than separate bullets.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences” aligns well with recent project work and current consulting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences,” “workflow automation,” and “CMS modernization” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Most tool names are repeated in “Technical + IT,” so avoid mirroring that section exactly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization” and repeats tools already proven in the recent Director role. Make this section more strategic and outcome-oriented, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a concise capability line: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and insight generation using GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Put higher-value capabilities before tools: lead with “KPI design,” “executive/leadership reporting,” and “optimization” rather than listing platforms first.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g. “analytics infrastructure for 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; consider keeping tools there and making this Topline Skills entry more strategic.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider folding into “optimization.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership-level event delivery rather than tool-like fragments.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio and control-room operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the studio build-out in the 2022–2024 role.
- Use parallel phrasing throughout; avoid mixing nouns (“Livestreaming”) with systems (“PTZ camera systems”).
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context tied to recent work, such as studio build-out or recurring advocacy programming.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- Tool-specific detail here overlaps with “Premiere Pro… Livestream studio workflows” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or removed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to show level of use, not just names: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize most relevant/recent platforms first and de-emphasize lighter-use tools: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint | Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider adding a qualifier only where defensible: “Drupal 10” if that version is central to recent work/projects
- Keep formatting parallel with other Technical + IT items; avoid a second generic CMS list if this section stays

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader platform skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied technical capabilities: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “for Drupal-based campaign sites, analytics setup, and workflow automation.”
- Put the strongest/current tools first: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless this section is strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actively build or lead.

Suggested edit
- Split by function and prioritize higher-value tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams” and drop lower-signal items unless heavily used.
- Rename to show capability, not just apps: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier: “Airtable (system design), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project workflows), Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination).”
- Order tools by strategic relevance and recency, not alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Basecamp and Trello may feel dated/redundant unless they were central in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic email/engagement leadership shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform depth without reading like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten and standardize the list: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation
- Consider a stronger version if format allows: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email automation • Segmentation • Newsletter operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications leadership already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience; keep this item platform-focused.
- Avoid repeating outcomes here that are already stronger in recent roles (e.g., newsletter reach, audience size).

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role clearly foundational: team build-out, early platform improvements, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and firsts: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft language: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific outputs like “produced livestreams, weekly video updates and campaign content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard/manage…” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- Avoid broad workflow/governance claims already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership and multimedia growth, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support plus the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Tighten generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with specific outputs if possible (e.g., articles, videos, interviews, campaign assets).
- If you can quantify, add scale: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audience/reach.
- Possible version: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy priorities, while producing digital and multimedia content. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize digital leadership here; save that progression for 2015–2024 roles.
